newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close weaker but off their lows.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close weaker but off their lows.

text.p: * NZ shares weaken as political uncertainty weighs on market
* Strong bonds offset equity weakness, shares end off lows
* GDP data in line with expectation, no impact on shares
Political uncertainty loomed large for New Zealand equities on Friday and saw them close the week and the quarter on an unsavoury note.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index fell 12.24 points to 2222.02, with all of the leaders posting losses on the day.
"I think the market was a bit unnerved by the poor performance of (Prime Minister Jim) Bolger on the leaders' debate last night," said John Rattray, director of equities at Ord Minnett.
In a televised debate between the leaders of the four main political parties, the Labour opposition took the honours.
As a result, brokers said the outcome of the October 12 election had been clouded even more and political uncertainty would increasingly prey on equities as the election neared.
However, a strong bond market had offset losses to some extent, with the market ending well off its intraday lows.
"It recovered on, among other things, a much better long bond rate, and perhaps an absence of any real selling," said Rattray. The top-40 index was at one stage more than 20 points weaker at 2213.44.
Brokers said gross domestic product data released this morning were within the band of expectation and had not had any effect on the market.
There had also been talk of fund managers "window dressing" softer stocks at the close of the quarter, but Rattray said the practice was going out of fashion.

"I think fund managers realise that if you trade a higher base at the end of one quarter, it makes performance more difficult in the next," he said. "I don't think there was any window dressing going on."
